newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hybrid seeds seen aiding Mexico's grain output.
newsitem.headline: Hybrid seeds seen aiding Mexico's grain output.

text.p: Hybrid seed varieties should help Mexico satisfy its grain demand which is expected to double in the next two decades, National Agriculture Investigation Institute director Jorge Kondo said on Monday.

Kondo, speaking at a conference here organized by the Mexico-based Sustainable Maize and Wheat Systems for the Poor (CIMMYT), said Mexico's advances in more drought resistant crop varieties would help keep up with growing grain demand.
Mexico will need to produce 60 million tonnes of grains by 2020, he said. Current output of 33 million tonnes is insufficient to satisfy demand of about 37-38 million tonnes.
The government has estimated Mexico will import about five million tonnes of grains for 1997, down from about 9.8 million tonnes imported in 1996.
"Crops of wheat, beans and cotton are done with improved seeds," he said.

Mexico's northern states has been plagued by devastating droughts in recent years, with many farming areas seeing woefully insufficient rainfall levels and others not reporting any rainfall for as long as three years.
Kondo said Mexico is now growing about 50,000 test hectares of a new variety of wheat that is highly resistant to drought. A new drought resistant pinto bean variety is also being tested.
But in corn, Mexico's largest crop and needed for human consumption as well as fodder, farmers have been slow to adopt advanced genetic hybrid seed varieties, Kondo said.
"In just 12 percent of Mexico's corn...is improved seed used," Kondo said.
"We need to incorporate the efforts you are making," he told the crowd of more than 400 scientists gathered for an international symposium on heterosis in crops.
Heterosis is the crossing two varieties of a plant that are very different to obtain a crop with a higher yield.

CIMMYT is an investigation center based in Mexico whose scientists work to improve mainly corn and wheat varieties, exporting information and technology around the world to improve farming conditions.
